title: Group pushes back on coffee tax
summary: A local coffee group has called out a proposal to impose excise taxes on coffee, warning that this could undermine the development of the country’s coffee industry.

blocks.text: A steaming cup of coffee on a bed of coffee beans.
MANILA, Philippines — A local coffee group has called out a proposal to impose excise taxes on coffee, warning that this could undermine the development of the country’s coffee industry.

In a statement, the Philippine Coffee Guild warned that any new tax on coffee could lead to higher retail prices, squeeze the margins of small roasters and affect the prices buyers can offer farmers for their harvests.
“It could show up in the price of a cup, in what a small roaster can afford to absorb or in what a buyer can offer a farmer for a harvest,” the group said.

The statement was issued after a representative of the Distilled Spirits Association of the Philippines suggested imposing excise taxes on coffee products, as alcohol consumption declines amid changing consumer preferences.

The coffee guild urged Congress and the Department of Finance to retain existing excise tax exemptions for coffee and to consult farmers, cooperatives, small businesses and other industry stakeholders before considering any new tax measure affecting the sector.
“Tax policy should support the people who grow it and keep it accessible to the people who drink it,” the Coffee Guild said.
The group also noted that coffee businesses already pay applicable income taxes, value-added tax or percentage tax and customs duties.
The group said alcohol and coffee should not be treated the same way under tax policies, noting that excise taxes are meant to curb consumption of products linked to adverse health outcomes.
